items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: you hear Tab Smith, and you hear just about everybody.

ctx.x: the way he played so beautiful, man. They never heard that kind of music in a saxophone. You know, you hear Johnny Hodges, you hear Benny Carter, you hear Earl Bostic, you hear Tab Smith, and you hear just about everybody. But you've never heard nothing in the classical veins like Leonard Fields.
There was a good saxophone player around New York that I happened to play with years ago named Jerome Pasquall. Did you ever hear him?

items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I’m with Lucky Millinder. Everybody’s talking about Lucky Millinder’s band. They got Tab Smith, Billy Kyle, Walter Johnson

ctx.x: I’m with Lucky Millinder for three years. We played everything between Duke and Cab. What they didn’t want, they shove in Lucky Millinder. Irving Mills was handling Lucky Millinder for a while. Lucky Millinder mess up with the money. Drank it. Throwed it away in the salary. They got mad with him. Said, “We got to get rid of this monkey.” So he never was a success no more, because you couldn’t trust him to bring the salary back in. That was the end of . . . So I’m with Lucky Millinder’s band. Lucky

Millinder’s hitting from here. Going, playing one-nighters here. Going to play a theater there and three or four one-nighters. He’s hitting and missing. He’s walking around all begging poor, but he done lost favor with the big dogs, the people who controlled everything. They said he’s . . . you can’t depend on him. I guess Lucky didn’t like it, people taking a big slice of his money. Some people just can’t stand that, but that’s a part of the game. Them people got to keep their offices going. They don’t mean to…
